messages:
jamie: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — capturing the budget & procurement Qs so folks who left early can catch up.

maria: can you confirm runway under the baseline vs downside scenarios? slides moved fast.

elaine: baseline ~18 months (current plan). downside with slower bookings + full hiring cadence ~13 months. we keep hiring-pause levers ready if needed.

matt: numbers: gross burn ~ $5.4M/mo today. baseline assumes revenue ramp lowering net burn to ~ $3.2M/mo by EOY. i'll upload the forecast sheet shortly.

jamie: @matt drop the link and call out which roles are "must-fill" vs deferrable so teams can plan.

matt: shared: https://short.link/redwood-budget-q2 (view-only). must-fill: 2 infra SREs, 1 security eng, 2 enterprise AEs. others can be deferred or backfilled later.

maria: procurement changes? vendor onboarding speed was a big ask from integrations.

devon: new rules go live next week: purchases >= $10k require finance + cost-owner signoff; >= $50k also needs an exec sponsor. default procurement card limit is $5k. Standard SLA 3 business days; new vendor onboarding up to 7 days.

maria: we have an urgent partner integration — 7 days is risky. any expedited path?

devon: yes — mark the PO with "expedite" and @devon + @finance-bot will triage. target 48-72 hours for true expedited cases but legal and security review still required.

jamie: can you paste the PO template so teams know what to fill out?

devon: snippet below:
```
PO Request fields: vendor_name, amount, cost_center, justification, contract_term, contact_email, expedite_flag
Approval flow: cost-owner -> finance -> exec (if >=$50k)
Target SLA: 3 bd (standard), 48-72h (expedite), up to 7 bd for new vendors
```

matt: small but important note on Dedicated reserved capacity: still supported but any new large commitments require a 9-12 month ROI business case (throughput uplift, cost/unit comparison, ops savings). i'll post a one-pager template.

jamie: request from eng leads: can finance publish a monthly one-slide snapshot with top 10 spend categories and a runway sensitivity table? helps planning across teams.

matt: yes — monthly snapshot will be posted in #finance and a short summary pinned in #all-hands with top vendors, committed Dedicated spend, and a hires sensitivity chart.

maria: card increases — process?

devon: team leads can request temporary card limit increases via the PO workflow. approvals based on cost center owner + finance.

jamie: final ask — can leadership post a 1-paragraph FAQ in #all-hands with the thresholds, card limits, and runway bullets for folks who missed the ending?

elaine: will post a pinned FAQ and a 90s Loom walking through the procurement flow tomorrow.

finance-bot: Procurement workflow updated 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z. Use /po-request to start. :robot_face:

jamie: thanks all — closing thread. :thumbsup:
